text: A hard little corn kernel goes into a hot pan. A few minutes later, pop! It turns itself inside out. How?
Look inside a popcorn kernel. A tough, shiny shell on the outside. Soft starch inside. And a little water, about fourteen percent.
As the pan heats up, that water turns into steam. But the hard shell won't let it escape. So the pressure builds.
At around one hundred and eighty degrees Celsius, the pressure inside is about nine times the air around us.
Then the shell bursts. The steam rushes out, and the soft, hot starch puffs up into a white foam that quickly sets.
Fun fact. That pop sound isn't the shell cracking. A twenty fifteen study found it comes from the steam escaping.
So why doesn't regular sweet corn pop? Its shell is weaker and leaky, so the steam just seeps out.
